about: Basic-level tutor follow-ups on questions from questions.json, written by gpt-6.1-sol (medium). The learner picked a wrong option.

items.question: You are abroad and discover that your passport is missing. You have already checked your bags and contacted the places you visited. Which organization should you contact about an emergency travel document?
items.correct: Your country's embassy or consulate.
items.picked: Your hotel's reception or concierge.
items.follow_up: Why is the hotel's concierge wrong if they regularly help foreign guests with emergencies and know the local procedures? I thought they could arrange an emergency travel document through the right authorities, especially if I don't know how to reach my embassy.

items.question: An electrician is preparing to replace a mains-powered wall socket. Which action is required before touching its conductors?
items.correct: Isolate the supply, prevent reconnection, and verify that the conductors are dead.
items.picked: Turn off the room's light switch and check that the ceiling light goes out.
items.follow_up: What if I turn off the socket circuit’s labelled breaker instead of the room’s light switch, and the ceiling light goes out? Would that be sufficient before touching the socket’s conductors, or must I still prevent reconnection and verify they are dead even if the circuit label is correct?

items.question: Two resistors of 4 Ω and 8 Ω are connected in series across an ideal 12 V DC source. What current flows through the 8 Ω resistor?
items.correct: 1 A
items.follow_up: I got 1.5 A by dividing 12 V by 8 Ω. Could you explain step by step why the 8 Ω resistor doesn’t have the full 12 V across it, and how the 4 Ω resistor affects its current even though we’re only asked about the 8 Ω resistor?

items.question: A circuit has a correctly sized cable and an ordinary overcurrent circuit breaker, but no residual-current protection. Which device detects an imbalance between outgoing and returning current and disconnects the circuit when that imbalance exceeds its operating threshold?
items.correct: A residual-current device (RCD).
items.picked: A miniature circuit breaker (MCB).
items.follow_up: Why is an MCB wrong here—if some current leaks to earth instead of returning through neutral, wouldn’t the MCB see that extra outgoing current as a fault and trip? I thought its magnetic trip mechanism would respond to that leakage even if the cable wasn’t overloaded.

items.question: With both ends of a wire disconnected from all equipment, a multimeter in continuity mode shows OL and does not beep when its probes touch opposite ends. The meter beeps when its probes touch each other. What does the wire test indicate?
items.correct: The wire has an open circuit between its ends.
items.picked: The wire has a low-resistance connection between its ends.
items.follow_up: What if the meter displays 180 Ω instead of OL across the wire, but still doesn’t beep, while touching the probes together still makes it beep? Would that indicate an open circuit, or a conducting path whose resistance is above the meter’s continuity-beep threshold?

items.question: You feel ill while traveling and want a pharmacist to recommend a nonprescription medicine. You have a known medication allergy. What should you do before accepting a recommendation?
items.correct: Tell the pharmacist which medicine you are allergic to.
items.picked: Choose a familiar package without checking its ingredients.
items.follow_up: If I’ve taken a medicine in a familiar package before without a reaction, why isn’t choosing it enough to avoid my allergy? Can you explain step by step how telling the pharmacist the exact medicine I’m allergic to helps them check whether a recommendation is safe, especially if brand names or ingredients differ while traveling?

items.question: Two lamps are connected in parallel to a suitable supply, each on its own branch. One lamp fails open-circuit, and no protective device trips. What happens to the other lamp?
items.correct: It stays lit with the same voltage across it.
items.picked: It goes out because the shared circuit is broken.
items.follow_up: If the failed lamp becomes an open circuit, its resistance is effectively infinite—wouldn’t that make the resistance of the whole circuit infinite and stop current through both lamps? I know there are separate branches, but why doesn’t an infinite resistance in part of the circuit force the total current to zero?

items.question: An ideal fixed resistor is connected to a DC supply. If the voltage across it doubles and its resistance stays constant, what happens to its power dissipation?
items.correct: It increases by a factor of four.
items.picked: It decreases by a factor of two.
items.follow_up: What if the resistance isn’t constant but instead follows R(V) = R₀[1 + (V/V₀)²]? If the DC voltage doubles from V₀ to 2V₀, by what factor does the power dissipation change?

items.question: Two lamps are connected in parallel across an ideal battery. One lamp fails so that its branch becomes an open circuit. What happens to the voltage across the other lamp?
items.correct: It remains at the battery voltage.
items.picked: It rises to twice the battery voltage.
items.follow_up: I thought that when one branch opens, the remaining lamp would get the voltage that had been shared between the two lamps, so its voltage would double. Can you explain step by step why voltage isn’t shared in a parallel circuit, and how the ideal battery keeps the voltage across the remaining lamp unchanged even though the total current decreases?

items.question: In standard Spanish, an adjective describes a group consisting of two women and one man. What gender and number must the adjective have under the conventional agreement rule?
items.correct: Masculine plural.
items.picked: Feminine plural.
items.follow_up: Why is feminine plural wrong when two of the three people are women? I thought agreement with a mixed group would follow the majority gender, so wouldn’t the two feminine members outweigh the one masculine member?

items.question: In standard Spanish, a learner writes "el agua frío" to mean "the cold water". Which correction is needed?
items.correct: Keep the article and make the adjective feminine.
items.picked: Make both the article and the adjective feminine.
items.follow_up: What if I move the adjective before the noun and write “el frío agua” instead? Would the correction still keep “el,” or does putting the adjective between the article and “agua” change which article is required?

items.question: A long cable run safely carries the load current, but the voltage at the equipment is below its permitted minimum because of cable voltage drop. The supply voltage and load must remain unchanged. Which change directly reduces this voltage drop?
items.correct: Increase the cable conductor cross-sectional area.
items.picked: Increase the circuit breaker's rated current.
items.follow_up: Can you walk me through why increasing the conductor’s cross-sectional area reduces the voltage drop when the load current stays the same, using the resistance and voltage-drop equations? I chose a higher-rated circuit breaker because I thought it would let more current through—why doesn’t its current rating affect the voltage lost along the cable?

items.question: A 6 Ω resistor is connected across an ideal 12 V DC supply. What current flows through the resistor?
items.correct: 2 A
items.follow_up: Why isn’t the current 72 A? I treated the 6 Ω value as the proportionality constant in I = kV, so 12 × 6 seemed right—why does resistance go in the denominator instead?

items.question: An electrician is about to replace a light fitting. The wall switch is off, but the circuit has not been isolated or tested. What should happen before work starts?
items.correct: Isolate the supply, secure it against reconnection, and prove dead.
items.picked: Check that the lamp is dark, then begin disconnecting its wires.
items.follow_up: What if the circuit has been isolated and locked off, and a two-pole voltage tester reads zero at the fitting, but the tester wasn’t checked on a known live source before the test? Can work start, or does the prove-dead procedure need to be repeated?

items.question: Two lamps must each receive the full voltage of a battery, and switching either lamp off must leave the other operating. How should the lamps and their individual switches be connected?
items.correct: Use parallel lamp branches, each with a series switch.
items.picked: Use one series lamp chain, each with a series switch.
items.follow_up: Can you explain step by step why putting the lamps in series fails both requirements, even if each lamp has its own switch? In the parallel arrangement, how does each lamp get the full battery voltage, and why does opening a switch in one branch not interrupt the current in the other?

items.question: A homeowner wants one hallway light controlled independently from either end of the hallway. Which conventional switch arrangement provides this without electronic controls?
items.correct: Two changeover switches linked by two traveller conductors.
items.picked: One changeover switch followed by one single-pole switch.
items.follow_up: Why is one changeover switch followed by a single-pole switch wrong if the changeover can divert the live feed to an unused throw and the single-pole can interrupt it downstream? I took “independently” to mean that either switch can turn the light off without touching the other, which this arrangement seems to allow.

items.question: A speaker says, “Ayer compré un libro.” How does the speaker present the purchase?
items.correct: As a completed event that happened yesterday.
items.picked: As a regular event that happens every day.
items.follow_up: If we change only “compré” to “compraba,” giving “Ayer compraba un libro,” does “ayer” still make the purchase a completed event, or does the imperfect leave its completion unspecified?

items.question: A circuit breaker has a short-circuit breaking capacity of 6 kA. The prospective short-circuit current at its installation point is 10 kA, and no manufacturer-approved backup protection is provided. What should be done?
items.correct: Use a breaker with a breaking capacity of at least 10 kA.
items.picked: Keep the breaker because its breaking capacity exceeds 1 kA.
items.follow_up: Can you explain step by step why the breaker’s 6 kA breaking capacity must be compared with the 10 kA prospective short-circuit current, rather than just checked against 1 kA? What could happen if the 6 kA breaker tried to interrupt that fault, and why does the lack of manufacturer-approved backup protection mean we need a breaker rated at least 10 kA?

items.question: You ordered one soup, but the bill charges you for two soups. You have not paid yet. What should you do first?
items.correct: Ask the server to correct the extra soup charge.
items.picked: Pay only for the soup and ignore other charges.
items.follow_up: If I know the price of the one soup I ordered, why can't I just pay that amount and ignore the remaining charges? Wouldn't that avoid paying for the extra soup without needing the server to correct an obvious mistake?

items.question: A speaker says, “El sábado pasado comieron en casa.” There is no additional context identifying the people. Which subject agrees with the preterite verb comieron?
items.correct: They, or you when addressing a group as ustedes.
items.picked: I, or you when addressing one person as tú.
items.follow_up: If the sentence were changed to “El sábado pasado comía en casa,” which subjects could agree with comía—could it now mean either “I” or “he/she/formal you”? Does “el sábado pasado” force a preterite interpretation, or can the verb still be imperfect?

items.question: A speaker says, “Trabajo en una oficina todos los días.” Which English translation best captures the meaning of the present tense here?
items.correct: I work in an office every day.
items.picked: I am going to work in an office every day.
items.follow_up: Could you explain step by step how “Trabajo en una oficina todos los días” expresses a present habit rather than a future plan? Is “todos los días” what makes the meaning habitual, or is it the verb form “trabajo,” and how would the Spanish sentence change to mean “I am going to work in an office every day”?

items.question: A technician calculates a resistor's power by multiplying the supply voltage by its resistance. The resistor is connected directly across an ideal DC supply, and only voltage and resistance are known. Which expression should replace that calculation?
items.correct: P = V²/R
items.picked: P = V²R
items.follow_up: Why is P = V²R wrong? I know power is I²R, and since Ohm’s law says current increases with voltage, wouldn’t substituting voltage for current give V²R while preserving the fact that higher resistance produces more heat?

items.question: Before leaving for school, a child says "Estoy listo." What does the child mean?
items.correct: I am ready.
items.picked: I am early.
items.follow_up: If the child says “Soy listo” instead of “Estoy listo,” would it mean “I am clever” rather than “I am ready”? Why would changing only the verb change the meaning of “listo”?

items.question: You leave your backpack on a city bus and notice it after the bus has departed. You are safe and have your phone. Which service should you contact first to try to recover it?
items.correct: The bus operator's lost-property service.
items.picked: The city's passport application service.
items.follow_up: Can you walk me through why the bus operator’s lost-property service is the first contact, especially if my passport might be inside the backpack? Why wouldn’t I contact the city’s passport application service first, and at what point would that service become relevant?

items.question: A machine has both a mains supply and a separate battery-backed supply capable of energising the parts being repaired. The mains isolator is locked off. What must happen before those parts can be considered safely isolated?
items.correct: Isolate and secure the battery-backed supply, then verify absence of voltage.
items.picked: Switch off the machine's display, then check that its screen stays dark.
items.follow_up: Why isn’t switching off the display and checking that it stays dark enough, if the battery-backed supply would also power the display whenever it was energising the machine? With the mains already locked off, wouldn’t a dark screen confirm that neither supply is delivering power?

items.question: A learner writes "el mano" to mean "the hand" in standard Spanish. Which change corrects the article?
items.correct: Use the feminine singular definite article.
items.picked: Use the masculine plural definite article.
items.follow_up: If I change the example from “el mano” to “el águila,” would I still need to replace “el” with “la,” or can “el” be correct even though “águila” is feminine?

items.question: A beginner says "Ana está médica" to mean that Ana is a doctor by profession. Which correction makes the sentence express that meaning in standard Spanish?
items.correct: Replace está with es to identify Ana's profession.
items.picked: Replace está with hay to identify Ana's profession.
items.follow_up: Could you explain step by step why “Ana es médica” identifies her profession, while “Ana hay médica” doesn’t work? I thought hay could mean that someone or something exists, so why can’t it say that Ana exists as a doctor, and how is that different from using ser or estar?

items.question: A friend says "El profesor es aburrido," rather than "El profesor está aburrido." What does the sentence with ser mean?
items.correct: The teacher is boring to other people.
items.picked: The teacher currently feels bored with something.
items.follow_up: Why is “the teacher currently feels bored” wrong if aburrido can mean “bored” and the teacher is the subject of the sentence? I thought ser could describe someone’s state without emphasizing a change, so wouldn’t está aburrido just make the temporary nature of the boredom more explicit?

items.question: A student argues that "Madrid está en España" is wrong because Madrid's location is permanent. Which response correctly addresses the mistake?
items.correct: Estar expresses geographical location, even when it is permanent.
items.picked: Both verbs express geographical location with the same meaning.
items.follow_up: What if the sentence were “Madrid es la capital de España” instead? Would estar still be required because this is geographical information, or does “la capital de España” change what the verb expresses?

items.question: Someone says "La reunión es en la biblioteca." Why is ser used here rather than estar?
items.correct: The sentence gives the location of an event.
items.picked: The sentence identifies the owner of a building.
items.follow_up: Can you walk me through why “La reunión es en la biblioteca” describes the location of an event rather than identifying who owns the building? I thought locations normally used estar, so why is it “La reunión es en la biblioteca” but “La biblioteca está en el centro”?
